extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX Coordinators, school employees, and legal/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Explanatory preamble to final Title IX regulations defining 'actual knowledge', reporting channels, Title IX Coordinator duties, supportive measures, and who triggers institutional response in elementary/secondary and postsecondary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge in elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual knowledge includes notice of sexual harassment to any elementary and secondary school employee (e.g., teacher, teacher's aide, bus driver, cafeteria worker, counselor, school resource officer, maintenance staff, or other school employee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice to any such employee charges the recipient with actual knowledge and triggers the recipient's response obligations. This expanded definition gives students a wide pool of trusted employees to whom they may report. Imputation of knowledge based solely on vicarious liability or constructive notice is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge for all recipients includes Title IX Coordinator notice
rubrics_metrics.description: For all recipients, the definition of 'actual knowledge' expressly states that 'notice' includes a report to the Title IX Coordinator as described in §106.8(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice to the Title IX Coordinator conveys actual knowledge and triggers the school's Title IX response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge in postsecondary institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the postsecondary context, actual knowledge requires notice to the Title IX Coordinator or an official with authority to institute corrective measures; notice to other employees does not automatically trigger the recipient's response obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is intended to respect college students' autonomy to control whether and when to report; institutions may still choose to require broader mandatory reporting internally but the regulations do not impose that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and contact information of Title IX Coordinator (§106.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must designate and authorize a Title IX Coordinator and notify all students and employees of the name or title, office address, electronic mail address, and telephone number of the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must prominently display the Title IX Coordinator's contact information on their websites and disseminate it to students, employees, and parents (for elementary/secondary). The Department expects clear, accessible reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt offering of supportive measures (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment, the recipient must promptly offer the complainant supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered irrespective of whether the complainant files a formal complaint. The Title IX Coordinator must contact each complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator contact obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact each complainant to inform them of the option to file a formal complaint and to discuss supportive measures (§106.44(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the complainant includes parents or legal guardians as appropriate in elementary/secondary contexts. The contact aims to ensure complainants understand options and available supports even if they decline to file a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures available without formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures must be available to complainants regardless of whether they file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer and implement measures designed to protect complainant safety, preserve equal educational access, and deter harassment while considering complainant preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to select an advisor of choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a grievance process has been initiated, recipients must provide parties written notice of each party's right to select an advisor of choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing precludes a complainant from choosing a friend or family member as their advisor; while the regulations do not expressly require allowing a supportive friend at the initial Title IX Coordinator meeting, they do not prohibit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may report and reporting channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (complainant, third party, witness, or the employee's/official's first‑hand observation) may give 'notice' that constitutes actual knowledge, and reports may be oral, written, anonymous, via news article, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.8 requires recipients to state that 'any person' may report and to provide multiple reporting modalities (phone, email, mail) including non-business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of reporting at any time
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports by phone or email may be made at any time, including during non-business hours, using the contact information listed for the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure reporting options are accessible beyond regular business hours and need not require scheduling an in-person appointment to convey notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere training or reporting obligation does not create authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere ability or obligation to report sexual harassment, to inform a student about how to report, or having been trained to do so does not qualify an individual as one who has the authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that trained employees or those with reporting duties are not automatically officials whose notice triggers institutional response, reducing imputation of knowledge solely because of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to train staff or require internal mandatory reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may train employees or impose their own mandatory reporting policies beyond what the regulations require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may choose to mandate that all employees report to the Title IX Coordinator; doing so does not cause the Department to impute greater notice to the recipient unless the employee actually gives notice to the Title IX Coordinator or an official with authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator training standards (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must receive training on how to serve impartially and without bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must ensure Title IX Coordinators do not rely on sex stereotypes and are prepared to offer supportive measures and explain formal complaint processes; the Department will hold recipients accountable for designating a properly trained Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal/clarification of 'responsible employee' rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not use the 'responsible employee' rubric from prior Department guidance and instead explicitly define who constitutes the Title IX Coordinator and officials with authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In elementary/secondary context, the need to identify 'responsible employees' is obviated because notice to any employee triggers response obligations; in postsecondary context, notice to officials with authority remains relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to institute corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may authorize any number of officials with authority to institute corrective measures; notice to such officials will trigger the recipient's response obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of which employees are officials with authority is a fact-specific inquiry; recipients have flexibility to designate who has that authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department accountability for recipients' response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will hold recipients accountable for meeting Title IX obligations, including for having an authorized, trained Title IX Coordinator and for responding appropriately when actual knowledge is conveyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Title IX Coordinator responds with bias or fails to take a report seriously, the recipient may have violated the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limitation on manner of receiving notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not limit how recipients may receive notice of sexual harassment; notice may be via oral report, written report, personal observation, newspaper article, anonymous report, or other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies across elementary/secondary and postsecondary contexts, subject to who receives the notice (any employee in K-12 vs Title IX Coordinator/officials in postsecondary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement to parents for elementary/secondary
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify parents of elementary and secondary school students of the contact information for the Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports accessible reporting and ensures families can locate the Title IX Coordinator for reporting or to obtain information about supportive measures.
